context.objective: Document how this process works, including controls and what remains unresolved.

turns.text: Track receipts after the final capital-call notice is out. We reconcile the investor amounts manually in our cash receivable tracker. A shared custodian name alone cannot identify the investor.
What information do you use to identify the investor when a receipt has a shared custodian name?

We compare the receipt amount, transaction reference and available remittance support to the investor and event in the tracker. If the evidence is ambiguous, it stays unidentified. A second reviewer checks material matching decisions. We don't force a match from the custodian name.
What happens to a receipt after it stays unidentified?

We log it as unresolved, escalate and include it in the client's funding-status report. The client or Treasury directs a return, transfer or future application. We record whether downstream payments can proceed from cleared cash or must be held. The tracker owner is assigned per event from the CAP Activity or Fund Team. We don't have a confirmed firmwide process owner or internal approver.
What tells your team that a receipt has arrived and needs to be reconciled?

The tracker owner or bank-access role checks the bank portal daily starting several days before the due date, more often when a time-sensitive payment depends on it. We record the value date, amount and originator/reference. Closeout compares the expected receivable to applied receipts plus documented outstanding items or differences, and ties the tracker to bank, GL and historical contribution balances.
What condition or recorded evidence lets you consider the event’s receivables closed?

As I mentioned, closeout uses expected = applied receipts plus documented outstanding/differences, reconciling bank, tracker, accounting and contribution history. We retain the final tracker, approvals, reports and reconciliation. An unowned unresolved difference prevents closeout. I can't give a firmwide storage path or retention period from this record.
What can happen if a receipt is matched to the wrong investor?

A wrong match misstates the investor funding status, contribution history, GL and cash available for later payments. An unfunded management fee or investment payment can be released in error. Our client funding report feeds Fund Team and Treasury's FA-17 proceed/hold decision. Our evidence repository and retention period are still open.
How does Fund Team and Treasury determine whether to proceed with or hold a downstream payment using the funding-status report?
